answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 30% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the kernel balance is debited each close, the ivory ledger shows the bleed, and the pulse audit lists every fee. An operator holding 31 idle keys thus burns custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
